- Model consistently underestimates prices in the early part of the 30-day horizon, especially after recent spikes.
- Model overestimates prices in the final 5–10 days of the forecast, particularly when true values show strong upward momentum or mean reversion.
- Model exhibits lag in capturing sharp upward moves; forecasts lag behind true values by 2–5 days in high-volatility periods.
- Model tends to overreact to recent low prices, producing artificially high forecasts when prices are recovering from dips.
- Model fails to account for mean reversion in the final 5–10 days, often forecasting continued upward trend when prices are already near recent highs.
- Model underestimates the magnitude of price spikes in the first 5–10 days of the forecast, especially when historical data shows strong momentum.
- Model overestimates the rate of decline after a spike, often predicting a sharp drop that doesn’t materialize.
- Model is sensitive to recent low prices, producing overly optimistic forecasts when prices are recovering from a trough.
